name: chat-stream
title: Chat stream
description: The room, in a frame that holds still. The height comes from the host, the same decision `stage` made, and the list inside is the only thing that scrolls, so a message arriving never moves the composer under the player's thumb. The pinned host message sits above the scroll and does not scroll away, one at a time. Two attributes carry the two ways a stream stops, because they happen to different people: `data-gs-following` absent is the player pausing it by reading, which stops the scroll while the room carries on, and `data-gs-paused` is the host freezing the room for everybody. A resumed stream marks what it missed with one centred line rather than replaying it. It stores nothing, ranks nothing and screens nothing: it scrolls itself to the foot while it is following, and reports the player scrolling away so the host can stop. `placement` is specimen 6i, the three ways chat fits a game screen while the screen holds still: `docked` is a fixed band at the foot of the interaction layer, `sheet` is the default and rises over the scene, and `overlay` floats the last few messages with no composer and no scroll. It is drawn as `data-gs-presentation` because the three differ in what the stream contains and not only in where it sits.
docs: Give it a height. It sets none and fills what it is given, so a stream in a box with no height collapses to its messages and the frame grows with the room, which is the failure `docs/mobile-game-frame.md` is about. Pass the messages as children, oldest first, each a `message`. `following` is yours: the stream reports `onPause` the moment the player scrolls away from the foot and `onResume` when they press the control, and neither changes anything by itself. `newCount` is what the resume control counts. `gap` draws the one line saying how many messages went past while the player was away; pass it when you resume after a long pause, and do not also pass the messages. `paused` is the host freezing the room, which is not the same as the player pausing it, and a stream can carry both. `placement` says which of specimen 6i's three treatments renders, and `docs/public/stage.md` says which stage layer each one belongs in. The default, `sheet`, draws no surface of its own: the panel, the scrim and the grab handle belong to the `sheet` component you wrap this in, so this item does not depend on it. A `docked` stream is the tallest thing the interaction layer holds and the 40% cap bites, which is GSUI-219: raise `--gs-stage-interaction-max` or the composer goes off the bottom. An `overlay` stream has no composer, does not scroll and reports no pause, because there is nothing to scroll back through.
